pr_body:
closes: #36270 

Avoid malicious scripts by escaping html tags in the different fields. This does not apply to the password because it is not a string field.

Previous attempt PR: #37316 

My previous attempt used a new validator to raise an exception if there were html tags, but now they are simply escaped. This allows the user to still put in the tags, but they will be showed as text instead of rendered (or worse executed in the case of a <script>)

Additionally, I have used the most recent version of the main branch possible to avoid the conflicts that were previously present.

Thanks again @potiuk and @hussein-awala for your feedback. Please let me know how I can improve this further

issue_context.title: Fix User name and other parameters potentially containing HTLM characters
issue_context.body:
### Body

The User name and other parameters should be  validated to not contain characters that might contain HTML-invalid characters. Also when they do, they should be escaped when rendered on HTML pages.

### Committer

- [X] I acknowledge that I am a maintainer/committer of the Apache Airflow project.
comments: Well. Part of the task is to find where it is.
I'm interested in working on this

Quick update:
I am working on a validator that checks for HTML tags to see if exceptions are raised correctly. From there, I will narrow the scope to raise exceptions in tags specific to XSS. Then, I will validate the text for invalid characters in HTML

review_comments: IMHO it would be better to add the expected output explicitly to ensure the escape works as expected. WDYT?
I can see the logic in that. It provides some transparency as to what escape is doing. 5 minutes

It is now added, but the test has been become slightly more brittle. If the escape from html is implemented differently the test may fail. Is it however based on a very stable standard. As such, I included both so the information is a bit more descriptive if it fails
